open_points.subject: A06 activation rule vs State 0 activation action
open_points.text: State 0: "an agent asking to activate a version with effects is refused and nothing is kept for the owner"; A06 rule 4: "Activating the version that is already active returns the active activation and records nothing, whoever asks."
open_points.question: If an effectful flow version is already active and an agent asks to activate that same version, must the request be refused or returned as success?
options: Always refuse agent requests for effectful versions (even if already active)
Return current activation for already-active version regardless of actor
open_points.default_guess: Return current activation unchanged for already-active version.

open_points.subject: A04 trial-case add rule vs State 0 capture action
open_points.text: State 0 allows capture by "owner, agent with author right"; A04 rule 1 says: "A trial case is added only by an agent with the author right".
open_points.question: Can the owner capture a failed execution into the trial corpus, or not?
options: Owner and authoring agent may capture
Only authoring agent may capture
open_points.default_guess: Allow owner and authoring agent to capture, per State 0 primary action.

open_points.subject: A16 authorization matrix
open_points.text: A16 rule 3 says permissions are "exactly the State 0 table" but its explicit list omits the "try implementation" action.
open_points.question: Who is authorized to call "try implementation" (owner, any agent, only may-author agent)?
options: Any agent
Only may-author agent
Owner and any agent

open_points.subject: Try operation semantics (K-11 surface includes "try")
open_points.text: State 0 defines action "try an implementation" but State 2 gives no normative rule for try scope/order/persistence.
open_points.question: What exactly does "try" execute (selected cases or whole corpus), in what order, and does it persist TrialExecution records or affect admission/activation state?
options: Run all current corpus cases in corpus order; persist evidence; no activation effect
Run caller-selected cases only; persist evidence
Run ad-hoc inputs without corpus linkage
open_points.default_guess: Run all corpus cases in corpus order, persist TrialExecution evidence, and do not change activation unless submitted for admission.

open_points.subject: A11 unknown-resolution trace vs A15 trace cardinality
open_points.text: A15 rule 1: "Every concluded attempt ... writes exactly one NodeExecution"; A11 rule 3: "An attempt therefore has at most two NodeExecutions: `outcome_unknown`, then the resolution's."
open_points.question: For one attempt that becomes unknown then resolved as applied, is there one NodeExecution or two?
options: Exactly one NodeExecution per attempt
Two NodeExecutions allowed for unknown->resolved(applied)
open_points.default_guess: Allow two NodeExecutions for unknown then applied-resolution, because A11 is specific to this case.

open_points.subject: Draft-write authority after unknown resolved not_applied
open_points.text: A10 rule 1: "`draft-write` nodes ask nothing at run time"; A11 rule 3 (`not_applied`): "the next send, under a fresh approval even where a grant exists".
open_points.question: If a draft-write attempt is resolved `not_applied`, must resend require owner approval (which draft-write normally never needs)?
options: Draft-write still does not require approval; resend proceeds without approval
All non-read resends after `not_applied` require fresh owner approval
open_points.default_guess: Keep draft-write no-approval behavior; require fresh approval only for classes that normally require approval.

open_points.subject: A05 fan-in constraints with constants
open_points.text: A05 phase 6 forbids only "no two edges that can both deliver" to one port, while phase 2 allows constants to node inputs.
open_points.question: Are multiple constants to one input, or constant+edge to one input, allowed; if allowed, how is the input value chosen/combined?
options: Refuse any port with more than one possible source (edge or constant)
Allow exactly one constant plus no delivering edge
Define precedence (constant overrides edge or edge overrides constant)
open_points.default_guess: Refuse any input port with more than one potential source, including constants.

open_points.subject: A05 phase 9 reach check wording
open_points.text: A05 phase 9: "every function node's output reaches a flow output or an operation node".
open_points.question: Does this require each output port of a function node to reach something, or only at least one output of that node?
options: Each output port must reach a flow output or operation node
At least one output port per function node must reach
open_points.default_guess: Require each output port to reach something useful.

open_points.subject: `stored_value_bytes_max` enforcement beyond run start
open_points.text: A20 defines `stored_value_bytes_max`; A12 checks it for flow-start inputs, but State 2 does not state checks/status for oversized values created as constants, trial values, function outputs, or service outputs before storing as StoredValue.
open_points.question: Where must `stored_value_bytes_max` be enforced, and what status/refusal is emitted in each context?
options: Enforce on every StoredValue creation; refuse authoring actions, fail runtime production
Enforce only on flow-start inputs
open_points.default_guess: Enforce at every StoredValue creation point; refuse author-time inputs and fail producing runtime node.

open_points.subject: Operation output spooling limit vs invocation outcome table
open_points.text: A15 rule 3: over `spool_file_bytes_max` or `spool_run_bytes_max` => producing node `resource_exhausted`; A09 table classifies 2xx output handling as `succeeded` or `contract_violation` with EffectAttempt `applied` for non-read.
open_points.question: For non-read 2xx responses whose file output exceeds spool limits, what NodeExecution status and EffectAttempt status are required?
options: NodeExecution `resource_exhausted`, EffectAttempt `applied`
NodeExecution `contract_violation`, EffectAttempt `applied`
NodeExecution `operation_failed`, EffectAttempt `unknown`
open_points.default_guess: NodeExecution `resource_exhausted` and EffectAttempt `applied` (effect may have happened).

open_points.subject: Owner refusal trace record details
open_points.text: A10 rule 3 says refusal ends run `refused`; M23 includes status `refused_by_owner`, but State 2 does not state explicitly which NodeExecution records are written at refusal time.
open_points.question: On owner refusal, which node/element gets a NodeExecution (`refused_by_owner`), and are other waiting elements recorded as skipped/upstream/refused?
options: Write one `refused_by_owner` record for the refused element only; leave others without new node records
Write `refused_by_owner` for all waiting effect elements
Write no NodeExecution for refusal event
open_points.default_guess: Write one `refused_by_owner` NodeExecution for the refused element only.

open_points.subject: Token uniqueness across owner and agents
open_points.text: A16 requires constant-time match against owner token and each agent token, but only agent names are constrained unique; token-value uniqueness is not stated.
open_points.question: If the same token value appears for owner and an agent (or two agents), is startup refused or is there a precedence rule for actor identity?
options: Refuse startup when any token value duplicates another
Define deterministic precedence (owner first, then agent order)
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup on any duplicate token value.
